episode_title: Brian Chesky on Founder-Led Mode, Design-Led Culture, and Scaling Airbnb
transcript:
Lenny: Welcome to Lenny's Podcast. Today my guest is Brian Chesky, co-founder and CEO of Airbnb. Brian, thank you for joining us.

Brian Chesky: Thanks for having me, Lenny. Great to be here.

Lenny: You recently spoke about moving Airbnb into what people are now calling 'Founder-Led Mode' after years of conventional management advice. What led to that pivot?

Brian Chesky: When Airbnb scaled to thousands of employees, conventional advice told us to hire experienced executives, delegate everything, and get out of the way. But by 2019, our product momentum slowed down, costs ballooned, and we were shipping org charts instead of cohesive products. I realized that a founder cannot simply delegate product vision. Founder-led mode means staying in the details, reviewing the product directly, maintaining tight control over user experience, and treating design as a core strategic discipline rather than a cosmetic polish.

Lenny: How did you restructure product development to support that vision?

Brian Chesky: We abolished traditional product management roles at Airbnb and merged product management with product marketing. We said product managers must be product marketers who understand the market, position the feature, and take full end-to-end accountability for driving adoption, not just writing PRDs. Secondly, we shifted to a single annual release roadmap where every team aligns on two major launch moments per year. This forced focus across the entire company.
